<span class="elementor-divider-separator">
</span></div></div></div><div class="elementor-element elementor-element-e2bc5d9 e-flex e-con-boxed e-con e-child" data-id="e2bc5d9" data-element_type="container" data-e-type="container"><div class="e-con-inner"><div class="elementor-element elementor-element-de35f9d elementor-position-block-start elementor-widget__width-initial elementor-view-default elementor-mobile-position-block-start elementor-widget elementor-widget-icon-box" data-id="de35f9d" data-element_type="widget" data-e-type="widget" data-widget_type="icon-box.default"><div class="elementor-widget-container"><div class="elementor-icon-box-wrapper"><div class="elementor-icon-box-icon">
<span class="elementor-icon">
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="e-font-icon-svg e-fas-wind" viewBox="0 0 512 512" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"></svg>				</span></div><div class="elementor-icon-box-content"><h3 class="elementor-icon-box-title">
<span>
One of the windiest spots in the world						</span></h3><p class="elementor-icon-box-description">
Few spots in the world boast as many days with winds above 25 knots: 20 to 25 knots in April and November; 25 to 32 knots in May and October; 30 to 35+ knots from June to September. 95% of the season's days are rideable.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="elementor-element elementor-element-0376348 elementor-position-block-start elementor-widget__width-initial elementor-view-default elementor-mobile-position-block-start elementor-widget elementor-widget-icon-box" data-id="0376348" data-element_type="widget" data-e-type="widget" data-widget_type="icon-box.default"><div class="elementor-widget-container"><div class="elementor-icon-box-wrapper"><div class="elementor-icon-box-icon">
<span class="elementor-icon">
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="e-font-icon-svg e-fas-water" viewBox="0 0 576 512" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"></svg>				</span></div><div class="elementor-icon-box-content"><h3 class="elementor-icon-box-title">
<span>
Flat water and waves at the same spot						</span></h3><p class="elementor-icon-box-description">
A large, shallow lagoon, ideal for learning and practicing tricks safely, and waves off the reef for experienced riders.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="elementor-element elementor-element-38a76f7 elementor-position-block-start elementor-widget__width-initial elementor-view-default elementor-mobile-position-block-start elementor-widget elementor-widget-icon-box" data-id="38a76f7" data-element_type="widget" data-e-type="widget" data-widget_type="icon-box.default"><div class="elementor-widget-container"><div class="elementor-icon-box-wrapper"><div class="elementor-icon-box-icon">
<span class="elementor-icon">
<svg aria-hidden="true" class="e-font-icon-svg e-fas-umbrella-beach" viewBox="0 0 640 512" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"></svg>				</span></div><div class="elementor-icon-box-content"><h3 class="elementor-icon-box-title">
<span>
The lodge right on the water						</span></h3><p class="elementor-icon-box-description">

<svg aria-hidden="true" class="e-font-icon-svg e-eicon-chevron-right" viewBox="0 0 1000 1000" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"></svg></div></div></div></div></div><div class="elementor-element elementor-element-8912772 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-parent" data-id="8912772" data-element_type="container" data-e-type="container"><div class="elementor-element elementor-element- elementor-widget elementor-widget-html" data-id="" data-element_type="widget" data-e-type="widget" data-widget_type="html.default"><div class="elementor-widget-container"><section class="kmg" style="max-width:1080px;margin:0 auto;padding:56px 20px;color:#0f1f35;font-size:17px;line-height:1.65"><h2 style="font-size:clamp(26px,3.2vw,38px);line-height:1.2;margin:0 0 16px">Kitesurfing in Madagascar: everything you need to know before you go</h2><p class="gt-block">Kitesurfing <strong>in Madagascar</strong> means sailing in one of the windiest spots in the Indian Ocean, at the island's tip, in Sakalava Bay, near Diego Suarez. Kitesurfing <strong>in Madagascar</strong> offers everything riders could want: consistent wind, a large, flat lagoon for safe progression, and waves breaking off the reef. <a href="https://sakalava.com/en/le-lodge/">Sakalava Lodge</a> is located right on the spot and houses the country's first IKO kitesurfing school, which opened in 2005.</p><h3 style="margin:28px 0 8px">When is the best time to go kitesurfing in Madagascar?</h3><p class="gt-block">The kitesurfing season in Madagascar runs from April to November, with winds gradually increasing until the heart of the southern winter. To choose the right month for your skill level, consult our guide to <a href="https://sakalava.com/en/blog/quand-partir-kitesurfer-a-madagascar/">when to go kitesurfing in Madagascar</a> and our <a href="https://sakalava.com/en/blog/kitesurf-madagascar-guide/">kitesurfing guide to Madagascar</a>.</p><h3 style="margin:28px 0 8px">Why choose Sakalava Bay for your kitesurfing holiday in Madagascar?</h3><p class="gt-block">The Sakalava Bay spot combines <a href="https://sakalava.com/en/blog/le-meilleur-spot-de-kitesurf-a-madagascar/">exceptional wind conditions</a> with easy logistics: bungalows, equipment, and a school are all just steps from the water. You can also try <a href="https://sakalava.com/en/wingfoil/">wingfoiling</a> during your stay, and our article <a href="https://sakalava.com/en/blog/kitesurf-ou-wingfoil-comment-choisir/">"Kitesurfing vs. Wingfoiling: How to Choose"</a> will help you decide.</p><h3 style="margin:28px 0 8px">An all-inclusive kitesurfing holiday in Madagascar</h3><p class="gt-block">Our packages include beachfront accommodation, full board, open bar, gym access, and, depending on the package, unlimited equipment. Find the details of <a href="https://sakalava.com/en/blog/sejour-kitesurf-wingfoil-tout-inclus/">what's included in an all-inclusive kitesurfing holiday</a> and all prices on our <a href="https://sakalava.com/en/tarifs-sakalava/">2027 kitesurfing rates</a> page.</p><h2 style="font-size:clamp(24px,3vw,32px);line-height:1.2;margin:40px 0 16px">Frequently asked questions about kitesurfing in Madagascar</h2><div style="margin:0 0 18px"><h3 style="font-size:19px;margin:0 0 6px">Where to go kitesurfing in Madagascar?</h3><p style="margin:0">The best kitesurfing spot in Madagascar is Sakalava Bay, in Diego Suarez (Antsiranana), in the far north of the island. Consistent wind, shallow lagoon for learning, waves off the reef for experienced kitesurfers: this is where Sakalava Lodge and its IKO Pro Kite School are located.</p></div><div style="margin:0 0 18px"><h3 style="font-size:19px;margin:0 0 6px">What is the best time for kitesurfing in Madagascar?</h3><p style="margin:0">The kitesurfing season in Madagascar runs from April to November. At Sakalava Bay, the wind blows 20 to 25 knots in April and November, 25 to 32 knots in May and October, and 30 to 35 knots and more from June to September, with approximately 95% of days being rideable during the season.</p></div><div style="margin:0 0 18px"><h3 style="font-size:19px;margin:0 0 6px">Is it possible to learn kitesurfing in Madagascar starting from scratch?</h3><p style="margin:0">Yes. Our IKO kitesurfing school, operating since 2005, offers 100% individual lessons, from the first time you've piloted the kite to waterstarts and then your first rides, in French, English, or Malagasy. Equipment is included as much as you like.</p></div><div style="margin:0 0 18px"><h3 style="font-size:19px;margin:0 0 6px">What does a kitesurfing holiday in Madagascar at Sakalava Lodge include?</h3><p style="margin:0">The all-inclusive stay includes the beachfront bungalow, full board, open bar, unlimited kitesurfing and wingfoiling (equipment, lessons, coaching) and the IKO certification offered at the end of the stay.</p></div><div style="margin:0 0 18px"><h3 style="font-size:19px;margin:0 0 6px">How much does a kitesurfing trip to Madagascar cost?</h3><p style="margin:0">Our all-inclusive 2027 packages start at €680 for 3 days/3 nights in a single bungalow, €1,400 per week for one person, and €2,400 per week for two people practicing kitesurfing in a double bungalow. Independent riders can stay from €130 per night.</p></div><div style="margin:0 0 18px"><h3 style="font-size:19px;margin:0 0 6px">Should you bring your kitesurfing equipment to Madagascar?</h3><p style="margin:0">No, it's not necessary: ​​the center has a complete and updated fleet (Airush range, Naish Expert 2027 range for rent). You can also bring your own equipment.</p></div><script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https:\/\/schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"Where to go kitesurfing in Madagascar?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The best kitesurfing spot in Madagascar is Sakalava Bay, in Diego Suarez (Antsiranana), in the far north of the island.
